name: ship-teardown-reconciliation
description: Issue #347: teardown as the ship ceremony's terminal gate — opened-resource manifest + reality-checked closing count (ship_teardown.py), immutable receipt (ship_receipt.py), certificate-gated merged-worktree reclaim with --if-idle, wired as the non-skippable terminal 'teardown' transition; release surfaces follow. Concurrency shaped to the operator cap of 3: U2 waits behind U1 (receipt embeds the reconcile report), U3 waits behind U1 AND U2 so its refute-3 panel (3 verifiers, at cap) never overlaps a running unit, U4's panel likewise runs alone; U5 is a lone haiku closer. Panels ride the unit tier (R4) on the two risky units only: U3 (removes worktrees — destructive semantics under the certificate) and U4 (wiring inside the #526-gated run() path, appends a transition to the canonical table).

units.label: ship_teardown.py manifest + reality-checked closing count + tests
units.prompt: U1: Create plugins/saga/scripts/ship_teardown.py (per-saga sidecar .claude/saga/sagas/<saga_id>/opened_resources.json per KTD2 with the #346 hardening — saga-id traversal guard, wrapped JSONDecodeError, atomic tmp+os.replace writes; register/close/read; reconcile() deriving the closing count with per-kind reality probes per KTD4, closed-but-alive entries flagged as discrepancies that count open; read-only 'reconcile' CLI verb printing CLEAN or HALT + named blockers) and the manifest/reconcile sections of tests/test_ship_teardown_reconciliation.py (test names follow test_AC_<n>_<scenario>). Read the plan at docs/plans/2026-07-11-issue-347-ship-teardown-reconciliation-plan.md (U1, R1/R2/R5, KTD2/KTD4) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: ship_receipt.py immutable writer/reader + tests
units.prompt: U2: Create plugins/saga/scripts/ship_receipt.py (mint() refusing on a non-zero closing count and creating .claude/saga/sagas/<saga_id>/ship_receipt.json via O_CREAT|O_EXCL then chmod 0444 per KTD5; ReceiptExistsError on re-mint; read() validates schema, never writes, and surfaces a named anomaly when recorded entries contradict a fresh reality probe) and the receipt section of tests/test_ship_teardown_reconciliation.py (AC3: mint-once, in-place mutation raises, receipt records every opened resource and its closed state; mint against non-zero count creates NO file). Read the plan at docs/plans/2026-07-11-issue-347-ship-teardown-reconciliation-plan.md (U2, R4, KTD5) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: reclaim subcommand: porcelain sweep, certificate gate, --if-idle + hook
units.worth_it_because: operator-escalated one rung: reclaim deletes worktrees and any missed skip-condition (dirty tree, unmerged head, detached HEAD) destroys uncommitted work — judgment tier for destructive semantics.
units.prompt: U3: Add the reclaim subcommand to plugins/saga/scripts/ship_teardown.py (sweep git worktree list --porcelain excluding the primary and the worktree it runs in per KTD6; skip dirty trees and unmerged heads with a report line; merged-ness via git merge-base --is-ancestor; removals require reversibility_certificate.authorize_write(WORKTREE_RECLAIM_MERGED) == AUTHORIZED per KTD7 — add that OpKind + OpFacts entry additively WITH its inverse descriptor (tests/test_reversibility_certificate.py's test_every_reversible_op_kind_has_registered_inverse iterates the registry); .saga-worktrees registry paths route through outcome_worktrees.reap_worktree; failed removals are kept and reported, never silently dropped; --if-idle <duration> no-ops while sidecar/registry mtimes are fresh AND applies the same bound per candidate worktree per KTD8 — a merged+clean worktree with recent activity is skipped in idle mode, the sibling-session guard), one additive SessionStart entry in plugins/saga/hooks/hooks.json invoking reclaim --if-idle 24h --quiet, and the reclaim section of tests/test_ship_teardown_reconciliation.py using real-git bare-origin fixtures (AC5 merged-vs-unmerged; certificate GATE monkeypatch removes nothing; dirty skip; recent-activity skip in idle mode; registry deregister; --if-idle fresh/aged). Existing tests/test_outcome_worktrees.py must stay green. Read the plan at docs/plans/2026-07-11-issue-347-ship-teardown-reconciliation-plan.md (U3, R6/R7, KTD6/KTD7/KTD8) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: ship_ceremony.py wiring: terminal teardown transition + register-on-open + receipt mint
units.worth_it_because: operator-escalated one rung: appends a transition to the canonical TRANSITIONS table inside the #526-gated run() path — a wiring mistake regresses the operator gate or the ledger-unadvanced refusal proof.
units.prompt: U4: Wire teardown into plugins/saga/scripts/ship_ceremony.py — append 'teardown' to TRANSITIONS and TRANSITION_TIERS (tier reversible, KTD3); _do_teardown in _RUNNERS runs reconcile with reality probes, attempts authorized closes for still-open ceremony-owned entries, re-reconciles, raises TeardownBlockedError naming every blocker BEFORE ship_undo.append_entry and the saga.py save on non-zero count (ledger provably unadvanced), and mints the receipt via ship_receipt on zero; register-on-open wiring per KTD9 (start() registers branch + draft PR, _do_open_pr registers the PR it creates, _do_merge closes the draft_pr entry, _do_branch_delete closes the branch entry); ship_undo gets a forward-only no-op handler for the teardown transition so undo never crashes on it. Extend tests: AC1 blocks_on_nonzero_closing_count, AC2 dry_run_halt_on_surviving_worktree, AC6 terminal_transition_not_skippable (TRANSITIONS[-1], next_transition('branch_delete'), seeded remote-delete-failed partial path), happy-path receipt mint + 'already shipped', pre-0.78.0 compat (saga at branch_delete reports teardown pending), undo no-op, and per-call-site register/close oracles; existing test_ship_ceremony.py assertions that end at branch_delete are updated deliberately. Read the plan at docs/plans/2026-07-11-issue-347-ship-teardown-reconciliation-plan.md (U4, R3/R4, KTD3/KTD9) as your authoritative spec.

units.label: release surfaces + journal (0.78.0)
units.prompt: U5: Bump plugins/saga/.claude-plugin/plugin.json to 0.78.0, sync the saga entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, add the [0.78.0] CHANGELOG entry (opened-resource manifest, closing-count teardown gate, immutable ship receipt, certificate-gated reclaim with --if-idle; call out that pre-0.78.0 ceremonies sitting at branch_delete regain one pending teardown transition), and update the drift-guard pin in tests/test_saga_plugin.py. The DECISIONS entry {#ship-teardown-terminal-gate-347} is already staged in the working tree — do not duplicate it; add a LEARNINGS entry only if implementation surfaced a non-obvious mechanism. Read the plan at docs/plans/2026-07-11-issue-347-ship-teardown-reconciliation-plan.md (U5, R8) as your authoritative spec.
